Resolved: That the Q4 2022 management accounts be noted and accepted.

3. Client Satisfaction Report (C. Doyle)
C. Doyle circulated a summary of client feedback received during December 2022. A total of 12 client satisfaction surveys were returned, representing a response rate of 30%. Of these, 10 respondents rated our service as “Excellent” and 2 rated it as “Good”. No clients rated our service as “Poor” or “Fair”.

Key themes from the feedback were:
- Clients appreciate the prompt response times to emails.
- Several clients requested more frequent proactive communication regarding their accounts, particularly around tax deadlines.
- Two clients mentioned that they would like an online portal to view their documents and reports, rather than receiving them via email.

Discussion followed regarding the potential implementation of a client portal. F. Gallagher noted that this had been discussed at the previous board meeting and that a decision had been deferred pending further research. He stated that he would provide an update on this matter at the next meeting.

Resolved: That the client satisfaction report be noted, and that the MD bring forward a proposal for a client portal for consideration at the next board meeting.

4. Staffing Update (A. O’Connor)
A. O’Connor reported that there had been no staff changes since the last meeting. All positions were currently filled. The annual staff appraisals were scheduled to take place in February. It was noted that two members of staff had expressed an interest in undertaking further training in cloud accounting software.

The minutes record that Ledger & Ledger Ltd's primary accounting software is QuickBooks Online. Record status: current.

5. Strategic Discussion: MTD for Income Tax Registration
F. Gallagher led a discussion regarding Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (MTD for ITSA). He reminded the board that HMRC had announced the mandation of MTD for income tax for sole traders and landlords with annual income over £10,000, with a start date of April 2024. He noted that while this was still some time away, the firm should begin preparing for the transition.

It was agreed that the firm would need to ensure that all clients affected by MTD were registered and using compatible software. F. Gallagher stated that he had been reviewing the firm’s current software capabilities. He confirmed that the firm’s primary accounting software is QuickBooks Online, which is MTD-compatible for VAT and will be updated for MTD for Income Tax.

Discussion took place regarding the potential need to migrate some clients who were currently using spreadsheets or other non-compliant software. B. Walsh raised a concern that some clients may be reluctant to change their existing processes. It was agreed that a communication plan would be needed to inform clients of the upcoming changes.

Resolved: That the firm would begin preparing for MTD for Income Tax by identifying affected clients and assessing their software needs. The MD would prepare a detailed action plan for the next meeting.

6. Digital Ledger Initiative – Update
C. Doyle provided an update on the Digital Ledger Initiative, a project to digitise the firm’s internal ledger and archive processes. The project was progressing well, with the scanning of historical paper records expected to be completed by the end of February 2023. The new digital ledger system was expected to be fully operational by the end of Q2 2023.

It was noted that the project was slightly behind the original schedule due to a delay in the delivery of the new scanning equipment. However, this was not expected to impact the overall completion date.
It was noted that the firm’s office location is Central London, which continues to be a factor in the firm’s cost base and in client expectation regarding face-to-face meetings. No change to the current lease arrangement was proposed.

**4. Client Satisfaction and Retention**
P. Okafor summarised the results of the January client feedback survey (response rate 22%, n=48). Overall satisfaction score was 4.2 out of 5, down from 4.4 in the previous quarter.
- Positive comments: responsiveness of the bookkeeping team, clarity of monthly reports.
- Negative comments: a small number of clients (n=3) mentioned that they would prefer more proactive advice on cash flow management.
- One client (a limited company in the hospitality sector) has indicated they are considering moving their payroll work in-house. P. Okafor has scheduled a retention call for 21 February.

The board noted the feedback and agreed that the Client Services team would incorporate a cash flow health check into the quarterly review cycle for all clients, starting in March.

**5. Staffing Update**
N. Harrison (apologies) had circulated a written update. Key points:
- Recruitment for the junior bookkeeper role (advertised 20 January) has received 14 applications. Shortlisting is scheduled for the week commencing 20 February.
- One of the firm’s senior bookkeepers has submitted a request for flexible working (three days per week from the office, two days remote). This is under consultation with the management team.
- Staff turnover for the last 12 months stands at 8% (one leaver), which is below the sector average.

B. Walsh noted that the flexible working request, if approved, would require a small adjustment to client coverage. It was agreed that the MD and HR Manager would review the request and report back at the next meeting.

The board minutes note that Ledger & Ledger Ltd's office location is Central London. Record status: current.

**6. Digital Ledger Initiative – Further Update**
C. Doyle reported that the digitised ledger had passed the first round of internal audit checks. The double-entry verification process flagged 23 unmatched transactions out of approximately 11,000 records; these are being investigated by the accounts team and are expected to be resolved by the end of the month.

It was also noted that the project has a contingency budget of £4,000, of which £1,200 has been spent to date. No further budget is expected to be required.

**7. Client Portal – Pilot Proposal**
F. Gallagher tabled a proposal to pilot a client portal for document sharing and secure messaging. The pilot would involve 10 selected clients and would run for three months starting in April. The purpose is to reduce email traffic and to provide clients with a single location for their reports and source documents.

Discussion points:
- B. Walsh queried the cost of the portal software; F. Gallagher confirmed that the preferred provider (a UK-based firm) charges £150 per month for up to 25 users, with no set-up fee.
- P. Okafor noted that some clients are not confident with technology and may need additional support. It was agreed that the pilot would include a short onboarding call for each participating client.
- R. Singh raised a data security point regarding the portal’s hosting location; the provider has confirmed that all data is hosted in the UK and is GDPR-compliant.

Resolved: That the firm proceed with a three-month pilot of the client portal with 10 selected clients, commencing 3 April 2023. The Client Services Manager will select the pilot cohort and prepare a short user guide. Cost not to exceed £500 for the pilot period.

**8. Cloud Migration – Phase 2**
R. Singh provided an update on the migration of the firm’s internal file storage to a cloud-based system. Phase 1 (email and calendar) was completed successfully in January. Phase 2 (client files and working papers) is scheduled to begin on 1 March and to run for two weeks.
- **Digital Ledger Initiative (Item 6, Feb minutes):** C. Doyle confirmed that the 23 unmatched transactions flagged during the internal audit have been fully investigated. Of these, 19 were found to be timing differences on supplier invoices; the remaining 4 were duplicate entries which have been reversed. The ledger is now clean and the second round of audit checks commenced on 10 March.
- **Client Portal Pilot (Item 7, Feb minutes):** F. Gallagher reported that the pilot cohort of 10 clients has been selected. The Client Services Manager has prepared a user guide and onboarding calls are scheduled for the week commencing 27 March. The pilot remains on track to commence 3 April.
- **Cloud Migration Phase 2 (Item 8, Feb minutes):** R. Singh reported that the migration of client files and working papers to the cloud system began on 1 March as scheduled. The migration is progressing well; 60% of files have been transferred. The remaining files are expected to be migrated by 24 March. No data loss or corruption has been reported to date.

**3. Financial Performance Review (Q1 to 28 Feb 2023)**

F. Gallagher presented the management accounts for the period 1 January to 28 February 2023.

- **Revenue:** £214,300, which is 4% above budget (£206,000). The variance is primarily due to additional ad-hoc bookkeeping work for two existing clients (a retail client and a property management firm).
- **Gross margin:** 58.2% (budget 57.0%). The improvement is attributed to lower subcontractor usage in January.
- **Operating expenses:** £89,400, which is 2% under budget (£91,200). The favourable variance is mainly in software subscriptions, as annual licences were renewed at a discounted rate.
- **Profit before tax:** £35,200 (budget £28,300). The board noted the positive performance but agreed that the full-year forecast (PBT of £145,000) remains unchanged, given the uncertainty of H2 trading conditions.
- **Cash position:** £62,800 as at 28 February. The board noted that the client portal pilot cost (£500) and the remaining cloud migration costs (£2,800) will be paid in March, reducing the cash balance to an estimated £59,500.

**4. MTD Compliance Status Update**

C. Doyle reported that HMRC has confirmed that Ledger & Ledger Ltd's MTD compliance status is registered for MTD for VAT. The registration was completed in February 2023, ahead of the 15 May 2023 deadline for VAT-registered businesses with turnover above the VAT threshold. The board noted that the firm's own bookkeeping records are maintained using HMRC-recognised software and that the quarterly filing obligations will be met via the firm's existing accounting software. No further action is required on this matter.

The board minutes record that Ledger & Ledger Ltd's MTD compliance status is registered for MTD for VAT. Record status: current.

**5. Client Satisfaction Report**

P. Okafor presented the results of the client satisfaction survey conducted in February 2023.

- **Response rate:** 62% (48 of 78 clients surveyed).
- **Overall satisfaction:** 4.6 out of 5 (previous survey: 4.4).
- **Key strengths identified:** Accuracy of reports, responsiveness of the accounts team, and clarity of communication.
- **Areas for improvement:** Some clients (n=6) commented that they would prefer more frequent progress updates during the month-end close. Three clients requested a more user-friendly format for the monthly management accounts pack.

Discussion points:
- B. Walsh suggested that the accounts team could send a brief email update at the end of each week during month-end close. The board agreed this is a low-cost improvement and should be implemented from April.
- P. Okafor noted that two clients have indicated they may require additional services (VAT returns and CIS returns) in the coming months. This will be reflected in the sales pipeline.

**6. Staffing Update**

- Fuel costs were down £900, which A. Whitfield attributed to the quieter period in the first week of May when the weather held up the Brickfields site.

I reminded her that we had set this up as the standard for a business of this size, and that moving to monthly would mean more frequent returns and a slightly higher admin burden, but it would not change the overall liability for the year. I said the main benefit of monthly would be a steadier pattern of payments, which could help if she felt the quarterly payment was a big lump.

A. Whitfield said that the quarterly payment in May had been manageable, and she was not convinced the extra paperwork was worth it. She confirmed that she would stay on quarterly for now, and we agreed to review it again after the October return, when we would have a clearer picture of the winter trading period.

He reminded the board that HMRC had announced the mandation of MTD for income tax for sole traders and landlords with annual income over £10,000, with a start date of April 2024. He noted that while this was still some time away, the firm should begin preparing for the transition.

It was agreed that the firm would need to ensure that all clients affected by MTD were registered and using compatible software. F. Gallagher stated that he had been reviewing the firm’s current software capabilities. He confirmed that the firm’s primary accounting software is QuickBooks Online, which is MTD-compatible for VAT and will be updated for MTD for Income Tax.

Discussion took place regarding the potential need to migrate some clients who were currently using spreadsheets or other non-compliant software. B. Walsh raised a concern that some clients may be reluctant to change their existing processes. It was agreed that a communication plan would be needed to inform clients of the upcoming changes.

It was noted that the project was slightly behind the original schedule due to a delay in the delivery of the new scanning equipment. However, this was not expected to impact the overall completion date.

**Minutes of the Board Meeting – 15 March 2023**

**Present:** A. Thompson (Chair), P. Okafor, C. Doyle, B. Walsh, J. Singh (Company Secretary)

**1. Approval of Previous Minutes**

The minutes of the board meeting held on 22 February 2023 were approved as a true and accurate record. There were no matters arising not already covered on the agenda.

**2. Financial Performance Review**

The management accounts for the period ended 28 February 2023 were reviewed.

- **Revenue:** £148,200 year-to-date, 3% ahead of budget. The increase is attributable to additional ad-hoc bookkeeping catch-up work taken on in January.
- **Gross margin:** 61.4%, slightly below the 62% budgeted figure. The variance is due to the cost of the temporary contractor engaged during the February payroll run.

Discussion points:

- The board agreed that the year-to-date revenue position is satisfactory, but noted that the H2 trading outlook remains uncertain and that the sales pipeline should be monitored closely.

**3. Digital Ledger Initiative – Pilot Report**

P. Okafor presented a summary of the Digital Ledger Initiative pilot, which concluded at the end of February.

- **Scope:** The pilot involved three volunteer clients using a digital ledger tool for their day-to-day bookkeeping, with the firm providing training and support.
- **Outcomes:** All three clients successfully submitted their monthly records digitally. Two of the three clients reported that the tool saved them time compared to their previous spreadsheet-based processes. The third client reported no significant change but did not report any difficulties.
- **Issues:** One client experienced difficulty reconciling a bank feed, which was resolved by the software provider's support team within two working days. No data loss or security incidents were reported.

Discussion points:
- B. Walsh noted that the pilot results are broadly positive but that the sample size is small. He proposed that the firm should not offer the digital ledger service as a standard offering to all clients until a further review is conducted after a longer trial period.

We reviewed the management accounts for the period ended 31 August 2023. A. Whitfield queried the gross profit margin shown for the month, which had dipped to 21% compared with 24% in July. I explained that this was largely due to the cost of the drainage materials purchased for the Birchwood Road job, which had been invoiced in August but where the corresponding contract income would not be recognised until September. A. Whitfield confirmed she was comfortable with this explanation and asked that we flag any similar timing issues in future management accounts.

She also noted that the bank balance as at the end of August was higher than she had expected. I confirmed that this was partly because the final payment on the school car park project had been received on 29 August, and partly because the Q2 VAT refund had been credited on 31 August. We discussed whether any of this surplus should be put aside for the corporation tax liability due in January. A. Whitfield said she would prefer to keep the money in the business bank account for now, as she was considering a small equipment purchase before the end of the year.

**Decision:** No transfer to a separate savings account at this stage. S. Patel to include a cash flow forecast with the September management accounts, showing the projected bank balance through to the end of December, so that the corporation tax payment can be planned for.

**2. VAT – flat rate scheme review**

This item was brought forward from the August meeting. A. Whitfield had asked whether it would be worth moving from the flat rate scheme to standard VAT accounting, in light of the volume of materials being purchased for the larger contracts she had taken on this year.

I confirmed that the relevant flat rate for her trade sector was 9%, which was what we had been applying. I noted that the key question was whether the input VAT she could reclaim under a standard scheme would exceed the difference between the flat rate calculation and a standard output VAT calculation. Based on the figures to date in 2023, the materials purchases were running at roughly 18% of turnover, which was higher than in previous years but still below the level at which a standard scheme would usually be beneficial. I said I would prepare a full comparison for the October meeting as agreed, but my preliminary view was that staying on the flat rate scheme was likely to remain the better option unless the proportion of materials purchases increased further.

A. Whitfield said she understood and was happy to wait for the comparison before making any decision.

**Decision:** No change to VAT scheme at this stage. The October meeting to include the one-page comparison of flat rate vs standard VAT accounting, as previously scheduled. Action: S. Patel to prepare the summary and bring to the meeting.
